svg.text: Test Automation: Benefits vs Risks
a tool does not guarantee success — benefits take effort; risks need analysis and mitigation
the pivot: analyze and mitigate the risks before the benefits pay off
Potential benefits
time saved on repetitive manual work — regression
runs, re-entering test data, result comparison,
checking against coding standards
fewer simple human errors — greater consistency
and repeatability in deriving and running tests
more objective assessment (e.g. coverage) plus
measures too complicated for humans to determine
easier access to test information for management
and reporting — statistics, graphs, aggregated data
shorter execution times — earlier defect detection,
faster feedback, faster time to market
more time to design new, deeper, more effective tests
Potential risks
unrealistic expectations about functionality,
ease of use — the tool's actual benefits
inaccurate estimates of time, cost, effort to
introduce, maintain scripts, change the process
using a tool when manual testing is more appropriate
over-reliance, ignoring human critical thinking
vendor dependency — vendor may go out of business,
retire or sell the tool, or provide poor support
open-source: may be abandoned, or its internal
components may need very frequent updates
tool not compatible with the development platform
tool not compliant with regulatory requirements
and/or safety standards
introducing a tool: run a pilot against agreed success criteria — roll out only if they are met
each new tool requires effort to achieve real and lasting benefits: introduction, maintenance, training
